title: Raw coordinate weighted-product obstruction for the finite Q3 quartic form
question: Does the raw coordinate multiplier q preserve the quartic Friedrichs form domain, or is K^(1/2) q K^(-1/2) necessarily unbounded?
method: Use the normalized translated Gaussian family with density variance 1/2 and generate all moments exactly from the centered Gaussian recurrence.
Compute the shifted onsite form energy E0(R)=q_K[psi_R] and the weighted energy E1(R)=q_K[q psi_R], including the derivative of q psi exactly.
Compare polynomial degrees and leading coefficients: E0 has degree four with leading coefficient g/4, E1 has degree six with the same coefficient, so E1/E0 is asymptotic to R^2.
Reproduce the samples independently and compile Lean R305 for the exact leading-coefficient ratio; retain bounded Lipschitz and resolvent-smoothed alternatives as separate routes.
finding: Primary 20/20, independent 18/18, integrated 13/13, and Lean R305 PASS. The raw coordinate route fails: E0 has degree 4, E1 has degree 6, and both leading coefficients are 3/20, so the normalized ratio E1/E0 divided by R^2 tends to 1. Therefore q does not preserve the quartic form domain with a uniform weighted bound, and K^(1/2) q K^(-1/2) cannot be bounded on this route.
decision_reason: This is a genuine route-local obstruction rather than a numerical near-miss. The quartic form controls q^4 but the weighted coordinate form requires q^6; the translated Gaussian witness makes the degree mismatch explicit. The result prevents promoting the raw coordinate to the weighted cylinder algebra, while leaving bounded Lipschitz and resolvent-smoothed polynomial routes available.
closed: exact Gaussian degree and leading-coefficient mismatch
independent reproduction and Lean R305 cross-check
bounded Lipschitz alternative retained as closed
open: other weighted algebras with higher powers of K
direct D and delta-D Cauchy estimates
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: All Gaussian moments and kinetic factors are generated from the declared variance; no sampled normalization is used.
The derivative of q psi is included; even with that contribution the weighted degree remains six.
Both leading terms are recomputed as g/4=3/20, giving an exact asymptotic ratio coefficient one.
The witness is one-site; adding nonnegative bonds cannot cancel the onsite q^6 growth.
Only the raw coordinate product is rejected; bounded Lipschitz and resolvent-smoothed polynomial classes are not decided here.
No QFT nonexistence or Clay conclusion follows; this is a named weighted-domain route obstruction.

qft_interface.closed: A route-local negative: raw coordinate multiplication is not a bounded weighted multiplier for the quartic shifted form.
qft_interface.open: Resolvent-smoothed polynomial cylinders, higher-weight alternatives, modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: This obstruction is not a production claim, heat_root_incidence, A1/R-192 owner, or Clay result.

next_action: Construct a resolvent-smoothed polynomial cylinder and test whether the resolvent commutator supplies enough decay to restore a K-form bound; if not, retain this obstruction as the stop condition for raw polynomial observables.
boundary: This is a route-local raw-coordinate weighted-product obstruction in the one-site quartic form. It is not an arbitrary-polynomial no-go, a common infinite-volume dynamics result, a QFT nonexistence theorem, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The failed route only excludes a uniform K^(1/2) q K^(-1/2) bound for the declared raw coordinate under the quartic form. Bounded multipliers, resolvent-smoothed polynomials and other weighted choices remain open.
